newsitem.title: USA: COMEX copper ends weaker, uncertain about spreads.
newsitem.headline: COMEX copper ends weaker, uncertain about spreads.

text.p: COMEX copper ended weaker in modest volume with the market nervous as dealers eyed the strong LME backwardation for signs of direction, dealers said.
The market is trying to find support at current levels, but much will hinge on what speculators decide to do, John Gross of the Copper Journal said.

"We have a lot of confusion out there. In part the weak price is a reflection of seasonal factors and reflects the speculative influence that has come into the market significantly in the past couple of weeks," Gross said.
Dealers said the squeeze on LME coupled with the seasonal slowdown was prompting some players to stay on the sidelines which cut volume and generated choppiness at times.
September COMEX copper settled 1.60 cents weaker at 104.70 cents a lb, traded 106.90 to 104.00 cents. Spot July went out 2.10 cents lower at 108.10 cents.
The LME cash to three months backwardation was at $245/$255 when COMEX closed, down $15 from the day's high.
The very strong backwardation was expected to continue drawing in large amounts of copper into LME warehouses, especially in the U.S. from COMEX depots, traders said.
Some dealers expected the tightness on LME to last through July while others believed it may ease sooner.
LME stocks rose 2,100 tonnes Tuesday to 143,300 tonnes.
COMEX stocks dipped sharply on Monday, down 2,379 short tons at 33,075 tons and were expected to shrink further.
Gross said the market has largely corrected from the sharp selloff last week, and conclusions could not be drawn from current prices.
"The tone is going to be set by the speculative side," he added.
